problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $3\times 3$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$

activity_context.topic_title: Solving Systems of Equations Using LU Factorization

feedback.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 7 & 1 & 0 \\ -9 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 7 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $3\times 3$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 7 & 1 & 0 \\ -9 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 7 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=9 \\ 7{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=7 \\ -9{y}_{1}+{y}_{3}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =9, \\ {y}_{2} & =7-7{y}_{1} \\  & =7-7(9) \\  & =-56, \\ {y}_{3} & =-1+9{y}_{1} \\  & =-1+9(9) \\  & =80.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
$y=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -56 \\ 80\end{aligned}].$
